finding.headline: You can count on $53,200 a year: $28,000 for basics and $25,200 for the rest.
details: Your basics cost about $28,000 a year.
The $52,000 goal works in 95 of 100 scenarios, but markets are uncertain, so this is not a promise.

assumptions: All figures are in today's dollars: what money buys now, not the larger sums prices will reach.

Savings grow on average 5.0% a year above inflation in stocks and 1.8% in bonds, with good and bad years. The plan tests many possible market paths. These are planning figures, not a forecast. They are fixed, so every plan is tested on the same markets; to see a bad stretch, try a What If such as markets fall 30%.
You already get Social Security (from 70): the plan uses the $30,000 a year you gave.

Tax uses the 2027 federal brackets, the standard deduction and your state's rates. In retirement the plan counts 85% of Social Security as taxable, the most the law allows, so the tax may be a little high.
The plan runs to age 93. There is about a 1 in 4 chance that you will live that long (US life table, SOA 2024). People with more money tend to live longer than that table says.

actions.title: Plan through age 93
actions.why: Age 93 is the planning horizon for your retirement money.

actions.title: Check your plan once a year
actions.why: Markets, prices and your own needs change. A yearly check keeps the plan close to the facts.

actions.title: Draw on taxable savings first
actions.why: Then pre-tax accounts, and Roth accounts last. That order usually keeps the tax bill lower.

worth_checking.title: An income annuity
worth_checking.why: You are one person with savings that may not last in a long life. An income annuity trades part of your savings for a fixed sum each year for life. The sum loses value to inflation and the money cannot be taken back. This is information only. This is something to look into, not a recommendation. I have not priced it.
